topicName: Memory Profiling, Asset Audit, and Cooked Build Size Reduction
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Memory Profiling, Asset Audit, and Cooked Build Size Reduction in Unreal Engine"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Optimizing memory consumption and reducing final package size are critical phases in Unreal Engine development. Bloated builds lead to longer load times, decreased framerates, and failed platform memory requirements. This tutorial covers advanced strategies for auditing assets, profiling RAM and VRAM, and leveraging cook-time configurations to shrink your packaged game."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Profiling Memory and Asset Footprints"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before reducing size, you must identify where memory is being consumed. Unreal Engine provides robust in-engine tools for capturing memory usage snapshots."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the command 'Stat Memory' in the console to view real-time breakdown of CPU, GPU, and RHI allocations."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Execute 'MemReport -Full' to generate a comprehensive report of all allocated memory, tracking down asset leaks and high-cost textures."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage the Size Map and Reference Viewer directly within the Content Browser to check the cumulative size of assets and their dependencies."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Utilizing the Asset Audit Window"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Asset Audit tool allows developers to review large collections of assets globally. Navigate to Window > Developer Tools > Asset Audit (or Asset Manager) to review texture resolutions, mesh poly counts, and material complexity across your entire project."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Consolidated command for asset metadata dumping: DumpUnusedAssets"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Reducing Cooked Build Size"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once resource hogs are identified, you can enforce strict packaging rules via DefaultEngine.ini to exclude unnecessary content and optimize compression."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"[Core.System]
Paths=../../../Engine/Content
Paths=../../MyGame/Content
Suppress=LogSerialization"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure Cooker Settings in Project Settings > Packaging to strip editor-only content and disable cooked maps from containing PIE (Play In Editor) metadata."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement Target Rules in your Target.cs files to disable plugins and features that your project does not utilize."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"bBuildDeveloperTools = false;
bUseLoggingInShipping = false;"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Texture and Audio Compression Optimization"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Textures and audio files typically make up the vast majority of a packaged game's footprint. Review texture compression settings (such as adjusting Max Texture Size and using ASTC/DXT compression formats appropriately per target platform) and convert uncompressed audio files (.wav) to compressed formats like Ogg Vorbis or ADPCM."},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"By routinely running memory reports, leveraging the Asset Audit window, and meticulously stripping unused developer tools and assets in your Target.cs configurations, you can dramatically lower your game's memory ceiling and packaged build size."}]
